t: LeetCode 1959 - Minimum Total Space Wasted With K Resizing Operations
o:
**Understanding the problem**

Between two resizes the array keeps one fixed size, so choosing sizes is the same as cutting the timeline into at most k + 1 contiguous blocks, each best sized to its block maximum. A block costs length * max(block) - sum(block), and the total waste sums this over blocks.

Examples:
- [10, 20], k = 0: one block sized 20 wastes (20 - 10) + (20 - 20) = 10.
- [10, 20, 15, 30, 20], k = 2: blocks [10], [20, 15], [30, 20] waste 0 + 5 + 10 = 15.

With n <= 200 and k < n, an O(n^2 * k) partition DP over (suffix start, resizes left) is comfortably fast; prefix sums make each block cost O(1) once the running max is known.
k: Resizing decisions partition nums into at most k + 1 contiguous segments, each charged len * max - sum.
Sliding a segment end by one updates its cost in O(1): new max, longer length, prefix-sum difference.
At most n * (k + 1) DP states exist and each scans up to n split points - tiny for n = 200.

a.i: dp(i, r) is the minimum waste for the suffix starting at i with r resizes remaining. With r == 0 the suffix must be a single block; otherwise choose the first block's end j, pay its cost, and recurse on (j + 1, r - 1). Memoization shrinks the search to at most n * (k + 1) distinct states.
s: Build prefix sums pre with pre[i] = nums[0] + ... + nums[i - 1].
dp(i, r): return 0 when i == n.
When r == 0 return max(nums[i:]) * (n - i) - (pre[n] - pre[i]).
Otherwise extend the first block to each j while tracking the running max, minimizing blockCost + dp(j + 1, r - 1).
a.t: O(n^2 * k) - each of the n * (k + 1) states tries up to n block ends
a.sp: O(n * k) - the memo table, plus recursion depth up to n

a.i: Define g[s][i] as the minimum waste covering the first i elements with exactly s segments. g[1][i] prices a single block; later rows append the last segment (p .. i - 1) to g[s - 1][p], maintaining that segment's max as p decreases. Forcing exactly k + 1 segments is safe: splitting a block never raises its cost, so the at-most-k optimum coincides.
s: Compute prefix sums; set g[1][i] = max(nums[0..i-1]) * i - pre[i].
For s = 2 to k + 1 and i = s to n: scan p from i - 1 down to s - 1 while maintaining max(nums[p..i-1]).
Relax g[s][i] with g[s - 1][p] + max * (i - p) - (pre[i] - pre[p]).
a.t: O(n^2 * k) - k layers of an n-by-n relaxation

w: Top-down is easier to defend in an interview; bottom-up avoids recursion limits. Key justification: within a block, sizing below the max breaks capacity and sizing above it wastes more, so len * max - sum is optimal per block. Pitfalls: forgetting the initial size is free (hence k + 1 blocks are allowed), overflowing 32-bit products (values reach 10^6 * 200), and misreading exactly versus at most k resizes. Follow-up: an O(n^2) divide-and-conquer or Monge-array optimization, or processing nums as an online stream.
